notes: B5 of eight chunks. The creator's Collabs tab — her whole working life in one place. Everything drawn from her side in B1 and B2, now as one coherent app.
her_six_stages_do_not_change: Invitations · Pitches · To sign · Shoot · Content · Done. They were built right and the new architecture does not touch them. What changes is what INVITATIONS MEANS: not 'someone wants to agree terms' but 'a whole deal has arrived'.
new_screens: The whole deal — one screen carrying the set's go-live day and mode, her money, what she can sell, her offer and her channels. Today this is two screens on two different days.
Her counter — money as the plain field; a different launch day and a different way of working marked optional and warned, because those move her out of the set.
Remote shoot — she sends the address. Does not exist today: the brand's side pre-fills it from her profile and she is never asked.
Go live — one row per channel she agreed, with the brand confirming each.
the_money_is_shown_before_she_agrees: A pay-for-content deal breaks the fee down 25/25/50 in rupees, with the wait named, on the invitation screen — not after signing.
empty_states_teach: Six stages, six different sentences. The deliverables empty state now explains WHY a commission creator has none — today it says 'No Deliverables Yet', which reads like a fault.
three_things_broken_or_missing: A live link has nowhere to live on a commission campaign. It is stored on a deliverable and she has none — 6 such creators, 0 deliverables, in production. 'Going live' is unrecordable for exactly the campaigns this platform is built around.
A commission collaboration cannot reach Done. Nothing computes completion without deliverables, so it sits at the shoot forever.
She cannot say where she will work — not in preferences, not on a pitch. Both need the same field, and B2's matching rule depends on it.
reliability_note: ⚠️ Her collab hub carried TWO separate crashes last week — a dead stage vocabulary and a React hook after an early return — and the button that opens the shoot had NO WORDS ON IT from the day Stage 4 shipped. This tab has the worst reliability record in the programme, and it is the one she lives in.
shared_backend_with_b2: The negotiation must hang off her row in a set rather than a standalone request. One piece of backend work serves both apps.

release.deploy_class: deploy-inert — mockups and specification only, no code

founder_answered_all_three.live_links: TWO RULES, by aim. Pay for content: one link per thing they bought, ALL required, each confirmed by the brand, and her second payment waits on them. Pay per sale: ONE link, for reference — "just a reference to him..just he uploads atleast one for reference how he is promoting his business" — gating nothing. Her money comes from her tracking link, not from this.
founder_answered_all_three.completion: TWO ENDINGS. Pay per sale: done when her content is live on social. The campaign itself runs on and keeps paying her — "no end for commission campaign but....till content submitted in socialmedia is completion of process". Pay for content: done when the FINAL payment for deliverables lands, after the admin-set wait. Neither ending is "when the deliverables run out", which is why nothing could compute it before.
founder_answered_all_three.where_she_works: On the PITCH, required, two answers — store visit or remote, no "either". "she has to mention clearly store visit or remote while pitching brand." NOT a standing profile setting: I had proposed one and it is wrong, because it is a per-deal answer. She may visit a shop down the road and want remote for one three cities away.

what_this_still_needs: All three answers land on the same missing piece: a place to record a live post that is NOT a deliverable. One table, one row per live post, per collaboration — required and countable for content, optional and singular for commission. Stage 4.
